Let the transpositions of \(\pi\) be the \(m=2q^2\) pairs
\[
P_1,\dots,P_m,\qquad n=2m=4q^2.
\]

For \(\sigma\in\Gamma\) with \(\pi_\sigma=\pi\), write
\[
\sigma(\rho_j)=\zeta^{c_j}\rho_j,\qquad
\sigma(\alpha_i^{(j)})=\zeta^{b_i^{(j)}}\alpha_{\pi(i)}^{(j)}.
\]
The condition \(\sigma(\rho_j)\ne \rho_j\) for all \(j\) is exactly
\[
c=(c_1,\dots,c_r)\in(\mathbb F_\ell^\times)^r.
\]

For a transposition pair \(P_a=\{i,\pi(i)\}\), define
\[
y_a=\bigl(b_i^{(j)}+b_{\pi(i)}^{(j)}\bigr)_{j=1}^r\in\mathbb F_\ell^r.
\]
This is independent of the chosen element \(i\in P_a\). Also, since \(\prod_i\alpha_i^{(j)}\in M\), applying \(\sigma^2\) gives
\[
\sum_{a=1}^m y_a=0.
\]

Now fix \(k\in\mathbb F_\ell^r\). On \(\Omega_k\),
\[
(i,h,u)\mapsto
\left(\pi(i),\pi(h),\,u+k c+b_i-b_h\right),
\]
where \(kc=(k_1c_1,\dots,k_rc_r)\). Squaring gives translation by
\[
2kc+y_a-y_b
\]
when \(i\in P_a\), \(h\in P_b\). Thus a \(2\)-cycle occurs exactly when this translation is \(0\).

Let
\[
A(x)=\#\{a:y_a=x\},\qquad 
F(v)=\sum_x A(x)A(x+v).
\]
Then the number of \(2\)-cycles on \(\Omega_k\), with \(v=2kc\), is
\[
C(v)=
\begin{cases}
\ell^r(2F(0)-m),&v=0,\\
2\ell^rF(v),&v\ne0.
\end{cases}
\]
Since \(c\in(\mathbb F_\ell^\times)^r\), the map \(k\mapsto v=2kc\) is a bijection of \(\mathbb F_\ell^r\).

The required differences force
\[
F(v)=F_O+4\ell(q+3Q)\mathbf 1_U(v)
+4\ell^2(q+Q)\mathbf 1_W(v)
+q^2\delta_0(v),
\]
where \(\dim U=r-1\), \(\dim W=r-2\). Summing over all \(v\) and using \(\sum_vF(v)=m^2=4q^4\) determines \(F_O\).

Taking Fourier transforms gives
\[
|\widehat A(\chi)|=
\begin{cases}
2q^2,&\chi=1,\\
q+4Q,&1\ne\chi\in U^\perp,\\
q+2Q,&\chi\in W^\perp\setminus U^\perp,\\
q,&\chi\notin W^\perp.
\end{cases}
\]
Because \(2\) generates \(\mathbb F_\ell^\times\), the primes \(q,q+2Q,q+4Q\) are inert in \(\mathbb Q(\zeta)\). Also \(2q\equiv1\pmod Q\), and \(\sum_a y_a=0\), so the root-of-unity ambiguity in each Fourier coefficient is forced to be trivial. Hence \(A\) is uniquely determined by the flag \(W\subset U\). Explicitly,
\[
A(x)=\frac{2q^2-q}{Q}-4+q\delta_0(x)+2\ell^2\mathbf 1_W(x)+2\ell\mathbf 1_U(x).
\]
Thus each flag \(W\subset U\subset\mathbb F_\ell^r\) gives exactly one conjugacy orbit for each \(c\in(\mathbb F_\ell^\times)^r\).

The number of such flags is
\[
\frac{\ell^r-1}{\ell-1}\cdot \frac{\ell^{r-1}-1}{\ell-1}.
\]
The number of possible \(c\)'s is \((\ell-1)^r\). Therefore the required number of \(\widetilde C_\pi\)-conjugacy orbits is
\[
\boxed{(\ell-1)^{r-2}(\ell^r-1)(\ell^{r-1}-1)}.
\]
